[b]Ohne Nachschub ist jede Armee verloren.[/b]
[i]Without supply, any army is lost.[/i] 

[spoiler=[b]Militärische logistische Vorbereitungen[/b]]

The Kaiserliche Marines grip over the seas surrounding the island allow the Reichswehrs supply ships to sealift supplies across the island. Under escort from the Kaiserliche Marine, dozens of Donnerkeil cruise missile batteries are brought into the island to add to the current supply. Roll/on roll/off ships at captured Sikirskian ports help bring in the carrier killer Seeschlange-26B missiles as well as dozens of naval strike missile batteries as the Reichswehr prepares to face the navies of Sikirsk and their allies. 

Other logistical considerations also come into play as the Reichswehr prepares for a long term engagement. Fuel for the J-16s, J-15Es, EK-70s and their accompanying AWACs are brought onto the island using fuel bladders while some longer range bombers still utilize well supplied bases in the mainland to continue their runs. Fuel farms at captured air bases and those on the mainland deliver a constant supply of aviation fuel, all heavily defended by air defense systems. 

On the ground the Engineer Korps works to repair and get the infrastructure the Reichswehr needs up to speed. Temporary air strips are established or preexisting ones are utilized to bring in K-30 cargo planes which drop ammunition, spare parts and sometimes vehicles. In higher threat zones, GPS-guided parachute systems are used to bring in the necessary supplies to continue the fight. Using the K-30s and roll/on roll/of craft large supplies of dried food are brought in to feed the troops while water is acquired using reverse osmosis units as well as water tankers. 

Wounded Reichswehr soldiers are taken care of as well. Quick MEDEVAC using the air forces vast supplies of helicopters bring the wounded quickly to role 2 and role 3 facilities. A typical wounded Kaiserreich infantryman in Nestor-Sikirsk can expect to be airlifted to a medical facility within fifteen minutes of contact. Using cold chain systems medications and blood are brought to the island via roll/on roll/off craft as well as aircraft. For the more seriously wounded they are given priority to fly back to more advanced hospitals in Neudresden which will give them spaces in the hospital upon request. Their Sikirskian counterparts, caught behind enemy lines and completely surrounded, can't expect the same. 

At sea the navy is kept well stocked and fed. Utilizing underway replenishment ships, navy ships can stay at sea for weeks. TRAM systems allow the Reichswehr to reload the missile stocks of guided missile cruisers and destroyers quickly. Following the engagement with submarines the TKS Seelowe carrier strike group conducts connected replenishment as well where ammunition, fuel, food and medical supplies are transferred from a logistics ship to the fleet. Trolley systems allow the supplies to move between the ships efficiently. [/spoiler]
